title: A Month of Buying Less
text:
After moving flat, I realised how many things I owned but rarely used. Three boxes of clothes stayed unopened, and I could not remember buying half the kitchen tools.

I decided to spend a month buying only food and other essentials. Whenever I wanted something new, I wrote it on a list instead of ordering it immediately.

The first week was difficult, especially when advertisements offered large discounts. By the second week, however, I had forgotten about most items on my list.

The experiment did not make me dislike shopping. It simply gave me time to notice the difference between needing something and wanting the feeling of getting it.
textTranslate:
搬家后，我意识到自己拥有很多很少使用的东西。三箱衣服一直没拆开，厨房里一半的工具，我甚至不记得是什么时候买的。

我决定用一个月时间，只购买食物和其他必需品。每当想买新东西时，我就把它写进清单，而不是立刻下单。

第一周很难熬，尤其是在广告给出大幅折扣的时候。不过到了第二周，清单上大多数东西都被我忘记了。

这个实验没有让我讨厌购物。它只是给了我一些时间，让我看清“需要某样东西”和“想要获得它时的感觉”之间的区别。

title: The Bicycle Repair Cafe
text:
On the first Saturday of each month, volunteers turn our community hall into a bicycle repair cafe. People bring broken bikes, share tea and learn how to fix simple problems.

I went there because my brakes were making a strange noise. I expected someone to repair them for me, but a volunteer handed me a tool and explained what to do.

It took longer than visiting a shop, and my hands became dirty. Still, when the wheel finally turned smoothly, I felt proud of a skill I had never thought I could learn.

The cafe is about more than saving money. It creates a place where asking basic questions is welcome, and where neighbours can become useful to one another.
textTranslate:
每个月的第一个周六，志愿者们会把社区活动厅变成自行车维修咖啡馆。人们带来坏掉的自行车，喝茶聊天，学习修理简单故障。

我去那里，是因为车闸发出了奇怪的声音。我原以为会有人替我修好，但一位志愿者递给我一件工具，并向我解释了操作方法。

这比去修车店花的时间更长，我的手也弄脏了。不过，当车轮终于顺畅转动时，我为自己学会了一项从未想过能学会的技能而感到自豪。

这家咖啡馆的意义不只是省钱。它创造了一个可以放心提出基础问题的地方，也让邻居们有机会彼此帮助。

title: An Unexpected Invitation
text:
I had lived in the building for six months without speaking much to anyone. We exchanged polite greetings in the lift, but everyone seemed too busy for a longer conversation.

One evening, a handwritten invitation appeared under my door. A neighbour on the fourth floor was organising a shared dinner, and guests were asked to bring any dish they liked.

I almost stayed home because I was worried about arriving alone. In the end, I made a simple salad and discovered that several other guests felt exactly the same way.

We did not suddenly become close friends. But now there are familiar names behind the doors, and borrowing a little sugar no longer feels like an impossible request.
textTranslate:
我在这栋楼里住了六个月，却几乎没有和任何人深入交谈过。我们在电梯里礼貌问候，但每个人似乎都忙得没时间多聊几句。

一天晚上，一张手写邀请函出现在我的门缝下。四楼的一位邻居正在组织一场聚餐，邀请大家各自带一道喜欢的菜。

我差点待在家里，因为担心自己一个人去会不自在。最后，我做了一份简单的沙拉，去了才发现，其他几位客人也有完全相同的担忧。

我们并没有突然成为亲密朋友。但现在，一扇扇门后都有了熟悉的名字，借一点糖也不再像是一个无法开口的请求。

title: Learning Together
text:
My friend and I started learning Spanish at the same time. She enjoyed grammar exercises, while I preferred listening to songs and repeating useful phrases.

At first, we tried to follow the same schedule. This quickly became frustrating: she thought I was moving too fast, and I felt that we spent too long on rules.

Instead of arguing about the best method, we chose one evening each week to practise together. We studied separately on other days and brought our questions to the meeting.

Our progress is not identical, but the arrangement works. Learning with someone does not have to mean learning in the same way; sometimes it means making room for different strengths.
textTranslate:
我和朋友同时开始学西班牙语。她喜欢做语法练习，而我更喜欢听歌并重复实用的短语。

起初，我们试着采用相同的学习计划。但这很快让人沮丧：她觉得我进度太快，而我觉得我们花在规则上的时间太多。

我们不再争论哪种方法最好，而是选择每周一个晚上共同练习。其他时间各自学习，把遇到的问题带到聚会中讨论。

我们的进步并不完全同步，但这样的安排很有效。和别人一起学习，不一定意味着用同一种方式学习；有时候，这意味着为不同的长处留出空间。
